subject: maths
question: Two trains are moving in the same direction at the speed of 40 km/hr and 90 km/hr, their lengths are 275 metres and 350 metres respectively. What will be the time taken by faster train to cross the slower train?
solution:
**Given:**

Speed of slower train = 40 km/hr

Speed of faster train = 90 km/hr

Length of slower train = 275 metres

Length of faster train = 350 metres

**Formula used:**

Relative speed when two objects move in the same direction = Speed of faster train - Speed of slower train

Time = Distance / Speed

**Calculation:**

Relative speed = 90 km/hr - 40 km/hr

⇒ Relative speed = 50 km/hr

Convert speed from km/hr to m/s:

⇒ Relative speed = 50 × (1000/3600) m/s

⇒ Relative speed = 50 × (5/18) m/s

⇒ Relative speed = 125/9 m/s

Total distance to be covered = Length of slower train + Length of faster train

⇒ Total distance = 275 m + 350 m

⇒ Total distance = 625 m

Time taken = Distance / Speed

⇒ Time taken = 625 / (125/9)

⇒ Time taken = 625 × (9/125)

⇒ Time taken = 45 seconds

**∴ The correct answer is option 1.**
